name: Roomba j7 and j7+
summary: The camera-navigating Roomba that promised to dodge pet accidents. Still common, still fixable, and its value now depends on what iRobot's new owner does with the app.
supportNote: iRobot filed Chapter 11 on 14 December 2025 and emerged on 23 January 2026 as a subsidiary of Shenzhen Picea Robotics. iRobot said app and support would continue. Check the current app status before paying for a used j7 that depends on the app for mapping.

symptoms.symptom: Runs for a few minutes, then returns to dock or dies

symptoms.cause: Dirty bin contacts or a bin that no longer registers

symptoms.symptom: Will not charge on the dock
symptoms.cause: Dirty charging contacts, dock power, or battery

symptoms.symptom: Clean Base will not empty the bin
symptoms.cause: Clogged evacuation path or full bag

symptoms.symptom: Gets lost, maps badly, camera errors in daylight-free rooms

buyChecks: Ask the seller to run it from the dock for ten minutes in front of you; watch for an early return.
Open the app on the seller's phone and watch them remove the robot from their account. Do not accept a factory reset alone.
Lift the bin and check the two metal contacts for corrosion.
Check the Clean Base bag and the evacuation port for a packed clog.
Confirm the dock, power supply, and at least one spare bag are included.
sellChecks: Run a full clean cycle, then empty and wash the bin and filter so the photos show a clean robot.
Remove the robot from your iRobot account in the app before handover, then factory reset.
Photograph the underside, the bin contacts, and the charging contacts; buyers of j7s ask about all three.
State the battery runtime you actually observed and the date you observed it.
Ship with the battery installed and the robot powered off; lithium batteries inside equipment ship more easily than loose packs. Check your carrier's rules.

name: Roomba i7 and i7+
summary: The first Roomba with the self-emptying Clean Base and persistent maps. Huge installed base, cheap parts, and the easiest Roomba to keep alive.
supportNote: Same ownership change as every Roomba: iRobot is now a Picea subsidiary after its January 2026 Chapter 11 exit. The i7 works as a button-press vacuum without the app, so an app outage is not a dead robot.

symptoms.symptom: Will not charge on the dock, or charges then dies
symptoms.cause: Dirty contacts, dock power, or worn battery

symptoms.symptom: Loud grinding from the brush area
symptoms.cause: Hair in the brush bearings or a worn brush module

symptoms.symptom: Drives in circles or one wheel drags
Dead, no lights, new battery does not help

buyChecks: Press CLEAN with the robot off the dock; it should start within a few seconds and run without an immediate error.
Watch the seller remove it from their account in the iRobot app.
Spin both drive wheels by hand; they should turn freely with slight resistance and spring back when pressed.
Look under the brush guard for hair wound into the bearings.
If a Clean Base is included, make sure it powers on and the bag door closes.
sellChecks: Replace the filter and side brush if they are visibly worn; it costs little and lifts the price.
Remove from your account, factory reset, and say so in the listing.
List the exact runtime you observed on a fresh charge.
Include the dock and power supply; a robot without a dock sells for parts money.
Pack the robot upright in its original foam if you kept it, or wrap the bumper so it cannot be pressed in transit.

name: Roomba 960
summary: A ten-year-old camera-mapping Roomba that still cleans. Parts are cheap and plentiful, but its used value is low enough that most repairs beyond a battery are not worth paying someone else to do.
supportNote: Old enough that app features may be reduced over time. Works as a button-press vacuum without the app.

symptoms.cause: Robot is stuck, or a wheel is not making contact

symptoms.symptom: "Error 6": stuck over a cliff or dirty cliff sensors
symptoms.cause: Dirty cliff sensors or a dark rug

buyChecks: Pay parts money only; a 960 that needs anything beyond a battery is not a bargain.
Confirm it starts, runs for five minutes, and returns to the dock.
Check the cliff sensor windows underneath for dirt and scratches.
sellChecks: Be upfront about age and runtime; buyers of a 960 are looking for a cheap second robot for one room.
Remove from your account and factory reset.
A 960 with a fresh battery and clean filter sells faster than one without; a battery costs less than the price difference in most markets.

name: Roborock S7 and S7 MaxV
summary: Lidar navigation, sonic mopping, and one of the biggest owner communities of any robot vacuum. Error codes are spoken aloud, which makes diagnosis easier than on most robots.
supportNote: Roborock numbers its error codes differently across generations. The verdicts below follow the Roborock Q7 Max manual table and the open-source python-roborock mapping, both of which agree for S-series codes 1, 3 and 4. Check your own manual if your robot says something different.

symptoms.cause: Obstruction on the lidar turret, or a turret that no longer spins
Dirty cliff sensor or a failed sensor

symptoms.symptom: Lidar turret does not spin, error persists after cleaning
Mop does not vibrate, or water does not flow
Dead after water ingress, board damage

buyChecks: Start it off the dock and listen: the lidar turret should spin up silently within seconds.
Ask the seller to delete the robot from their Roborock app in front of you.
Look at the water tank seal and the mop plate clip; both wear and both are cheap but tell you how it was treated.
Run it over a dark rug edge for a minute to prove the cliff sensors are not confused.
Confirm the dock type: standard, Auto-Empty, or Empty Wash Fill. They are not interchangeable.
sellChecks: Clean the lidar window and the cliff sensors; the first five minutes of a buyer's test decide the sale.
Delete the robot from your app and reset Wi-Fi.
State which dock is included and whether the mop module is present.
Drain the water tank completely before shipping.
Ship with the battery installed and the robot off; tape the bumper so it cannot be pressed in transit.

name: Roborock S8 Pro Ultra
category: Robot vacuum and mop with dock
summary: A flagship with a dock that washes, dries and refills. Expensive new, which is exactly why a two-year-old one is the most interesting used robot in the category.
supportNote: Dock faults are the most common reason an S8 Pro Ultra is sold. Many dock problems are a clogged filter or a dry pump rather than a dead dock.

symptoms.symptom: Dock will not wash or dry the mop
symptoms.cause: Clogged dock filter, empty clean-water tank, or pump

buyChecks: Run one full mop-wash cycle at the dock in front of you; it is the most expensive part to replace.
Ask the seller to remove the robot from the Roborock app.
Check the dock's clean-water tank for scale and the dirty-water tank for smell; both tell you about maintenance.
Confirm the dock ramp, mop pads, and dust bag are included.
sellChecks: Run a dock self-clean, empty and dry both tanks, and replace the dust bag before photos.
Delete the robot from your app.
Photograph the dock interior; serious buyers ask for it.
Ship the dock and robot in separate boxes if you still have them; the dock is heavy enough to damage the robot in one box.

name: Ecovacs Deebot X1 Omni
category: Robot vacuum and mop with dock
summary: Ecovacs' first all-in-one station robot, with a voice assistant built in. Sold in large numbers, now turning up used as owners upgrade.
supportNote: Ecovacs documents its error messages in the app rather than as spoken numeric codes. The symptoms below are the ones owners report most; we have not yet performed these repairs ourselves and the rows say so.

symptoms.symptom: Station will not wash mops or refill
symptoms.cause: Empty clean tank, clogged filter, or pump

symptoms.symptom: Main brush stalls, brush error in app
Lidar error, robot spins in place

buyChecks: Run one station wash cycle in front of you.
Watch the seller remove the robot from their Ecovacs account in the app.
Check the station tanks for scale and smell.
Confirm the mop plates and dust bag are included.
sellChecks: Run a station self-clean, empty both tanks, and replace the dust bag before photos.
Remove the robot from your Ecovacs account and reset Wi-Fi.
Ship the station and robot separately if possible.

name: Unitree Go2
summary: The most widely owned legged robot outside a lab. Its used market is where the used-humanoid market will be rehearsed first: licence tiers, firmware, and actuator wear decide value more than cosmetics.
supportNote: Go2 trims (Air, Pro, EDU) differ in what the owner is allowed to do with the software. A used Go2 is only worth the EDU premium if the EDU licence demonstrably transfers. Ask Unitree before paying for it.

symptoms.symptom: A leg is weak, hot, or clicks
Will not connect to app or SDK
Fall damage to shell or lidar

buyChecks: Ask for the exact trim (Air, Pro, EDU) and proof of what the software licence allows a second owner to do.
Watch it stand, walk, and recover from a push; listen for clicking from any leg.
Ask for the actuator temperature readout after five minutes of walking.
Confirm the number of battery packs and the charger are included; spare packs are a large share of the value.
Ask whether the robot was ever opened or firmware-modified.
sellChecks: State the trim, firmware version, and what you were told about licence transfer.
Record a short video of a stand, walk, and push recovery; it answers most buyer questions.
Count and state battery packs and cycles if the app shows them.
Ship batteries according to your carrier's lithium rules; these packs are large enough to need the proper label.
